task.brief: Investigate GetRepoPermissions in this Gitea revision. Compare a normal authenticated caller querying their own collaborator permission with the same caller querying another user's permission; include differences for privileged callers visible in source. Explain path-specific controls, identity comparison and the repository permission result. Follow upstream code only when relevant. Do not turn this behavior question into an invented normative policy.

rules.claim: The GET collaborators/{collaborator}/permission route enters GetRepoPermissions.
The route invokes GetRepoPermissions for GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{collaborator}/permission.
The target identity is taken from the collaborator path parameter.
The request is rejected when the doer is not an admin, the collaborator path name does not case-insensitively equal the doer's LowerName, and the doer is not a repository admin.
A non-admin, non-repository-admin caller querying a different collaborator name is denied with HTTP 403 before target-user lookup or permission calculation.
If any of the three authorization alternatives holds—global admin, case-insensitive self-name match, or repository admin—the handler continues to look up the named collaborator.
After successful target lookup and repository-permission calculation, the handler returns HTTP 200 JSON containing the named collaborator and permission.AccessMode via convert.ToUserAndPermission.
